question: A decomposed data-processing workflow requires Claude to invoke dozens of small tools in a tight loop, and issuing each call through the standard conversational tool-use turn is adding significant latency and token overhead. Which technique addresses this?
options: A) Wrap each tool invocation in its own subagent so the orchestrator only sees final results, reducing calls the primary agent must track
B) Use programmatic tool calling so Claude invokes tools directly from a code execution container, cutting round trips and token overhead per call
C) Increase the effort parameter on the primary model so it plans calls further in advance and needs fewer conversational turns to finish
D) Batch all tool calls into a single Message Batches request so the many small invocations execute asynchronously outside the conversation
correct_answers: B) Use programmatic tool calling so Claude invokes tools directly from a code execution container, cutting round trips and token overhead per call
explanations: Incorrect. Wrapping every small tool call in its own subagent adds orchestration and reporting overhead rather than removing the per-call round-trip cost within a tight loop.

Correct. Programmatic tool calling lets Claude call tools directly from code running in a code execution container, avoiding a full conversational round trip per call and reducing latency and token consumption for tight, multi-tool loops.
Incorrect. Raising effort increases reasoning depth per turn but does not change how many separate conversational turns are needed to issue a large number of small tool calls.
Incorrect. Message Batches is for asynchronous, large-volume request processing, not for reducing round trips within a single live, tightly looped tool-calling workflow.
